**29**

The goal is to guarantee at least one round apple + one star peach, or at least one round peach + one star apple (i.e., both flavors present with opposite shapes).

To find the minimum guaranteeing number, first compute the largest number drawable *without* satisfying the condition, then add 1.

The sets that avoid the condition are:
- Only watermelons (8 round + 4 star) = 12
- Only apples (7 round + 7 star) + all watermelons = 14 + 12 = 26
- Only peaches (9 round + 6 star) + all watermelons = 15 + 12 = 27
- Apples and peaches both round only (7 + 9) + all watermelons = 16 + 12 = 28
- Apples and peaches both star only (7 + 6) + all watermelons = 13 + 12 = 25

The largest avoiding set is 28 (all round apples, all round peaches, all watermelons). In this set there are both flavors but same shape, so neither matching pair exists.

Any draw of 29 must include at least one star apple or star peach (the only remaining candies). Adding a star apple to the 28 creates round peaches + star apples. Adding a star peach creates round apples + star peaches. Either way the condition is met.

Thus 29 is the smallest number that guarantees the requirement in the worst case.

**29**

To guarantee having either (round apple + star peach) or (star apple + round peach), consider the worst-case scenario that avoids both combinations. This requires satisfying both of these logical conditions simultaneously:  
- (0 round apples OR 0 star peaches)  
- (0 star apples OR 0 round peaches)  

Watermelon candies (round: 8, star: 4) can always be included, as they do not affect the condition. The maximum under the avoidance constraints is achieved by taking all 7 round apples, all 9 round peaches, and all 12 watermelon candies (total: 28). In this set:  
- Star peaches = 0, so (round apple and star peach) is impossible.  
- Star apples = 0, so (star apple and round peach) is impossible.  

Any additional candy must be a star apple or star peach:  
- Adding a star apple (with round peaches present) triggers the second combination.  
- Adding a star peach (with round apples present) triggers the first combination.  

Thus, 28 candies can be taken without the required combinations, but 29 guarantees at least one of them.

**29**

To determine the minimum number of candies that guarantees the condition (having either at least one round apple and one star peach, or at least one round peach and one star apple), first identify the maximum number of candies that can be taken *without* satisfying the condition. This is found by maximizing the sum of the relevant counts while ensuring the negation holds: \((A_r = 0 \lor P_s = 0) \land (P_r = 0 \lor A_s = 0)\), where \(A_r, A_s\) are round/star apples (max 7 each), \(P_r, P_s\) are round/star peaches (max 9 and 6), and watermelons (irrelevant to the condition) are maximized at 12.

The configurations satisfying the negation and maximizing the total are:

- Set \(A_r = 0\), \(A_s = 0\): take all peaches (15) + all watermelons (12) = 27.
- Set \(A_r = 0\), \(P_r = 0\): take all star apples (7) + star peaches (6) + watermelons (12) = 25.
- Set \(P_s = 0\), \(P_r = 0\): take all apples (14) + watermelons (12) = 26.
- Set \(P_s = 0\), \(A_s = 0\): take all round apples (7) + round peaches (9) + watermelons (12) = 28.

The maximum without the condition is 28 (e.g., all 7 round apples, all 9 round peaches, all 12 watermelons). Adding any further candy (a star apple or star peach) would activate one of the OR terms, satisfying the condition.

Since 28 is achievable without the condition but any selection of 29 must exceed this maximum (as all apples/peaches total only 29 and cannot be fully taken without triggering the pairs), 29 is the minimum that guarantees the condition in the worst case.

**29**

To guarantee having at least one apple candy and one peach candy of different shapes (i.e., either at least one round-apple paired with at least one star-peach, or at least one star-apple paired with at least one round-peach), calculate the worst-case number you can draw without this happening, then add 1.

The ways to avoid both cross pairs are:
- No apples at all (max: all 15 peaches + all 12 watermelon = 27)
- No round apples and no round peaches (max: all 7 star-apple + all 6 star-peach + all 12 watermelon = 25)
- No star peaches and no star apples (max: all 7 round-apple + all 9 round-peach + all 12 watermelon = 28)
- No peaches at all (max: all 14 apples + all 12 watermelon = 26)

The largest of these is 28 (all round apples, all round peaches, all watermelon). In this set you have round apples and round peaches but neither cross pair is present (no star apples, no star peaches).

Any 29th candy must be either a star apple or a star peach. In either sub-case the cross pair is created:
- Adding a star apple gives star-apple + round-peach.
- Adding a star peach gives round-apple + star-peach.

Thus 29 is the minimum that forces the condition in every possible draw.

**29**

To determine the minimal number of candies to draw to guarantee the condition, calculate the maximum number that can be drawn *without* satisfying it (i.e., without having both (round apple and star peach) or (round peach and star apple)), then add 1. The candies that do not affect the condition are the watermelons (8 round + 4 star = 12 total), which can always be included.

The condition requires taking at least one from each of the two pairs {round apple, star peach} and {round peach, star apple}. To *avoid* the condition while maximizing the draw, take exactly one from each pair (plus all watermelons). This yields four options:

- Round apple (7) + round peach (9) + watermelons (12) = 28  
- Round apple (7) + star apple (7) + watermelons (12) = 26  
- Star peach (6) + round peach (9) + watermelons (12) = 27  
- Star peach (6) + star apple (7) + watermelons (12) = 25  

The maximum without the condition is therefore 28 (all round apples, all round peaches, and all watermelons). Any draw of 29 must include at least one star peach or one star apple on top of this selection. Adding a star peach creates round apple + star peach; adding a star apple creates round peach + star apple. In all other avoiding selections, the 29th candy forces the same trigger.

Thus, 29 is the smallest number that guarantees the required combination in every possible case.
